data.title: Data Type
data.tagline: A data type is the format agreement for one piece of information: text, number, date, or an on/off value.
data.learningOutcome: You can assign a fitting type to each field in a list and name the cost of a wrong type (no summing, no sorting).
data.description: If the amount field is a number type, phones show a numeric keyboard and records can be summed; stored as text, it can neither compare nor total. A date type opens a date picker and enables time sorting. The type fixes the format before entry, while validation checks at submit—two things that happen in order.

learning.assumes: You know some form inputs only accept digits and some open a date picker.
learning.outcome: You can assign a fitting type to each field in a list and name the cost of a wrong type (no summing, no sorting).

distinctions.label: Field
distinctions.explanation: Field answers "what to record"; Data Type answers "what format that information takes".

distinctions.label: Data validation
distinctions.explanation: Data Type agrees on the format before entry; Validation checks the submitted value against rules.

explanation.title: Number
explanation.text: A numeric keyboard on entry; the list can sum and compare. Amounts, quantities, and stock should be numbers.

explanation.title: Date
explanation.text: Phones open a date picker with one consistent format; sorting and filtering by time work. Typing dates by hand is text and none of this works.

explanation.title: Choice
explanation.text: Pick from fixed options such as "following up / won / archived" instead of everyone wording their own.

data.boundary: A type is the format agreement before entry; data validation is the check at submit—the type blocks most format problems and validation catches the rest. "Amount" is a field name; "number" is its type. A phone number looks numeric but never needs summing, so a text type serves better—the test is "will I compute on it later," not "does it look like a number."

lessonPractice.title: The quote tool needs to "sort by date." Which type should the date field use?

options.label: A date type
options.feedback: Correct. A date type sorts chronologically and opens a date picker on phones, avoiding messy formats.

options.label: A text type, typing "Mar 2" manually
options.feedback: Text cannot be ordered in time: "Mar 2" and "Dec 1" sort wrongly as text, and formats drift.

options.label: A number type, entering 0302 for March 2
options.feedback: Packed numbers lose month and day information; sorting and display both break. Dates belong in a date type.

data.agentPrompt: Check the field types: amount as a number, date as a date picker, status as a fixed set of options. Amount seems stored as text and cannot be summed; after fixing the types, try summing and sorting by date.
